body.statement: There is a universal \(L<\infty\) such that for every admissible sequence, \[\Pr_{G_n}\!\left\{\|B_{G_n}P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\right\}\longrightarrow1.\]
body.justification: This graph certificate is the missing input that would turn the inherited log-tuned seed construction into a high-probability upper bound over every admissible degree sequence.
body.gap: The sparse branch and the dense Boolean-polynomial truncation are proved. The dense grouped Charlier operator estimate and the centered row-sum component are not; Xu's stated single-shape theorem does not provide them at the prescribed moment order.
body.consumer: If proved for the full right-projected operator, this theorem would discharge the graph event used by the established seed-risk theorem and finite compiler.

obligation.what_is_open: In the dense subrange \(n^{2/5}\le d_n=o(\sqrt n)\), prove a high-probability bound for the full right-projected operator \(\|B_{G_n}P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\). The simple-completion factorial moments and the Boolean-polynomial truncation error are now proved, but the grouped polynomial contribution and its row-sum component remain open.
obligation.obstruction: Xu (2025), Sections 2.2--2.3, does not furnish the requested estimate. Its theorem concerns one edge-character graph matrix at a time, while its block-value proof takes absolute edge values and sums nonnegative step-label costs, so it cannot preserve cancellation between the Charlier blocks of \(Q\). Its regular-graph walk lemma also assumes \(\log n\ll q\), whereas the prescribed \(\ell=\lceil10\log n/\log\log n\rceil\) satisfies \(\ell/\log n\to0\). Independently, the proposed moment of \(P_n(Q-\mathbb EQ)P_n\) controls only the sandwiched operator; it omits the term \(n^{-1/2}\|P_n(Q-\mathbb EQ)\iota_n\|_2\) needed for the right-projected norm. No frozen result controls that term.
obligation.attempted: I proved the marked residual-completion switching bound for \(\mathbb E(C_{12})_m\) uniformly through \(m=2K+2\), derived the exact alternating-binomial remainder, and used the falling-factorial product identity to obtain \(n^2\mathbb E(B_{12}-Q_{12})^2\le n^{-18+o(1)}\). I then checked the primary Xu theorem and its block-value proof at theorem level, expanded the projection decomposition, and reran the exhaustive eight-vertex cubic enumeration. The enumeration reproduces all five rational probabilities and the signed moment, but it has no asymptotic force.
obligation.partial_result:
Work on an arbitrary subsequence satisfying
\[
n^{2/5}\le d=d_n=o(\sqrt n),\qquad \eta=\frac{d^2}{n},
\qquad h=\log(1/\eta).
\]
By \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), eventually \(0<\eta<1/2\).  Put
\[
K=\left\lceil\frac{20\log n}{h}\right\rceil,
\quad C_{ij}=(A_{G_n}^2)_{ij},
\quad S_K(c)=\sum_{r=1}^K(-1)^{r+1}\binom cr,
\]
and, for \(i\ne j\),
\[
Q_{ij}=(A_{G_n})_{ij}+\{1-(A_{G_n})_{ij}\}S_K(C_{ij}),
\qquad Q_{ii}=1.
\]
The alternating-binomial identity
\[
\sum_{r=0}^K(-1)^r\binom cr=(-1)^K\binom{c-1}{K}
\quad(c>K)
\]
and the full binomial identity when \(1\le c\le K\) give, deterministically,
\[
|(B_{G_n})_{ij}-Q_{ij}|
=\{1-(A_{G_n})_{ij}\}\binom{C_{ij}-1}{K}
  \mathbf 1\{C_{ij}>K\}.
\tag{1}
\]

Here is a completion-switching proof of the factorial-moment input, without conditioning a configuration model on simplicity.  Let \(H\) be a simple partial graph of maximum degree at most \(d\), let \(r_v=d-\deg_H(v)\), let \(R=\sum_v r_v\), and let a completion be a simple graph \(F\), edge-disjoint from \(H\), having degree sequence \((r_v)_v\).  Fix \(u\ne v\) with \(uv\notin E(H)\).  Partition the completions into \(\Omega_1\) and \(\Omega_0\) according as \(uv\in E(F)\) or not.  For \(F\in\Omega_1\), orient an edge \(xy\in E(F)\), delete \(uv,xy\), and insert \(ux,vy\).  Of the \(R\) oriented edges, at most \(4d\) have a vertex coincidence with \(u\) or \(v\), at most \(d^2\) have \(ux\in E(H\cup F)\), and at most \(d^2\) have \(vy\in E(H\cup F)\).  Every other choice is a simple, edge-disjoint completion in \(\Omega_0\).  Conversely, a completion in \(\Omega_0\) has at most \(r_ur_v\) inverse choices, obtained by choosing the residual neighbor \(x\) of \(u\) and the residual neighbor \(y\) of \(v\).  Double counting therefore yields
\[
\Pr\{uv\in E(F)\mid H\}
\le \frac{|\Omega_1|}{|\Omega_0|}
\le \frac{r_ur_v}{R-2d^2-4d}
\tag{2}
\]
whenever the denominator is positive.  If \(\Omega_0\) were empty, the positive number of forward switchings would itself be a contradiction, so (2) also covers that case.

For an integer \(1\le m\le 2K+2\), expand \((C_{12})_m\) as the sum over ordered distinct witnesses \(w_1,\ldots,w_m\in V_n\setminus\{1,2\}\).  Conditional successively on the \(2m\) edges of the copy of \(K_{2,m}\) rooted at \(1,2\), apply (2).  Since \(h\ge\log 2\), one has \(K=O(\log n)\); since \(d\ge n^{2/5}\), eventually \(2K+2<d\).  With
\[
\delta_n=
\frac{2d^2+4d+4(2K+2)}{nd}=o(1),
\]
every switching denominator is at least \(nd(1-\delta_n)\).  The residual-degree numerators multiply to \((d)_m^2\{d(d-1)\}^m\).  Label exchangeability and \((n-2)_m\le n^m\) consequently give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E(C_{12})_m
&\le
\frac{(n-2)_m(d)_m^2\{d(d-1)\}^m}
     {\{nd(1-\delta_n)\}^{2m}}\\
&\le \eta^m(1-\delta_n)^{-2m}
=\{1+o(1)\}^m\eta^m.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The error is uniform over \(m\le2K+2\), and its logarithm is at most \(4m\delta_n=o(Kh)\), because \(m=O(K)\), \(\delta_n=o(1)\), and \(h\ge\log2\).  This proves the requested factorial-moment estimate directly under the uniform simple regular law.

Let \(r=K+1\).  From (1),
\[
|(B_{G_n})_{12}-Q_{12}|^2\le\binom{C_{12}}r^2.
\]
The exact product identity
\[
(c)_r^2=\sum_{j=0}^r\binom rj^2j!(c)_{2r-j}
\]
and (3) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\binom{C_{12}}r^2
&=\sum_{j=0}^r
  \frac{\mathbb E(C_{12})_{2r-j}}{j!(r-j)!^2}\\
&\le \eta^r\exp\{o(Kh)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed, after extracting the uniform switching-error factor, the sum has at most \(r+1\) terms, every factorial denominator is at least one, and \(\eta^{2r-j}\le\eta^r\); moreover \(\log(r+1)=o(Kh)\).  Since \(Kh\ge20\log n\), while \(d\ge n^{2/5}\) gives \(h\le(1/5)\log n\) and hence \(Kh\le(101/5)\log n\), (4) gives
\[
n^2\mathbb E\{(B_{G_n})_{12}-Q_{12}\}^2
\le n^{-18+o(1)}=o(d^{7/2}).
\tag{5}
\]
The diagonal of \(B_{G_n}-Q\) is zero, so exchangeability, (5), and Markov's inequality yield
\[
\|(B_{G_n}-Q)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\|B_{G_n}-Q\|_{\mathrm F}=o_{\Pr}(d^{7/4}).
\tag{6}
\]

Thus the switching/truncation part of the prescribed dense argument is complete.  The remaining grouped trace estimate is not supplied by the cited Xu theorem.  In that source a graph matrix \(M_\tau\) is attached to one fixed shape and is a sum of monomials in centered edge characters.  Its Section 2.3 block-value proof first bounds the absolute edge value for each shape walk and then sums nonnegative step-label costs.  It therefore does not retain cancellation between distinct Charlier blocks.  Moreover, the source's regular-graph edge-value lemma assumes \(\log n\ll q\ll d^{1/10}\), and its Section 2.2 theorem requires \(q=\Omega(|U_\tau|\log^c n)\) for a sufficiently large constant \(c\).  The prescribed order
\[
\ell=\left\lceil10\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right\rceil
\]
satisfies \(\ell/\log n\to0\), so it does not satisfy the cited trace-order hypothesis.

There is also a separate deterministic gap between the displayed estimate and the desired right-projected norm.  If \(H=Q-\mathbb EQ\), then
\[
HP_n=P_nHP_n+(I_n-P_n)HP_n,
\qquad
\|(I_n-P_n)HP_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=n^{-1/2}\|P_nH\iota_n\|_2.
\tag{7}
\]
A trace bound for \((P_nHP_n)^{2\ell}\) controls only the first term in (7).  The second is not zero because regularity of \(G_n\) does not make the radius-two or truncated-Boolean row sums constant.  The logical implication cannot hold for symmetric matrices in general: for any nonzero \(v\perp\iota_n\), the symmetric matrix \(H=\iota_nv^{\mathsf T}+v\iota_n^{\mathsf T}\) has \(P_nHP_n=0\) but \(HP_n=\iota_nv^{\mathsf T}\ne0\).  A sufficient grouped estimate would instead bound
\[
\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}
\left[\{P_n(Q-\mathbb EQ)^2P_n\}^{\ell}\right]
\]
at the corresponding scale, or would supplement the displayed sandwich moment by
\(n^{-1/2}\|P_n(Q-\mathbb EQ)\iota_n\|_2=o_{\Pr}(d^{7/4})\).  Neither estimate follows from the frozen primitives or from Xu's stated single-shape theorem.

For the mandated finite check, exhaustive enumeration of all \(19{,}355\) labeled cubic graphs on eight vertices again gives
\[
p=\frac{513}{553},\quad a=\frac{475}{553},\quad
b=\frac{16771}{19355},\quad t=\frac{15493}{19355},\quad
s=\frac{2059}{2765},
\]
and hence
\[
s-4pt+p^2(4a+2b)-3p^4
=\frac{360638638}{467595722405}.
\]
This verifies the finite identity but supplies neither the missing signed grouped moment nor the row-sum estimate.
